subject: english-language
topicDisplay: Paper 1 Non Fiction Texts And Transactional Writing
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the assessment objectives.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A travel article says "You will love every breathtaking moment of this paradise." What is its main PURPOSE?
options: To argue against tourism
To give scientific data
To complain
To persuade the reader to visit
questions.explain: Positive, emotive language directed at "you" is designed to persuade the reader to go.

questions.q: What is the best way to structure a piece of persuasive writing for impact?
options: Put every idea in one giant paragraph
Save the main point for a footnote
List random facts in no order
Open with a hook, develop arguments in clear paragraphs, end with a memorable call to action
questions.explain: A strong structure hooks, develops logically and ends with a powerful closing message.

questions.q: Which technique is being used: 'Imagine a world where no child goes to bed hungry'?
options: Direct address and an emotive appeal
An anecdote
A statistic
A rhetorical question
questions.explain: It speaks directly to the reader ('Imagine') and triggers an emotional response.

questions.q: Which sentence is the strongest, most memorable ending to a persuasive piece?
options: The choice is yours: act now, or watch our future slip away.
That is the end of my writing.
I think I have said enough now.
So yeah, that's about it really.
questions.explain: A direct, balanced final appeal leaves a lasting impression on the reader.

questions.q: Which sentence opener creates the most engaging, dramatic story opening?
options: The door slammed shut behind me, and the lights went out.
I am going to tell you about a time I was scared.
It was a normal day at school.
My name is Tom and this is my story.
questions.explain: Starting in the middle of the action (in medias res) hooks the reader immediately.

questions.q: To SYNTHESISE information from two sources, you should:
options: List every word in both texts
Ignore the second source
Quote only the first source
Combine relevant points from both into a single, linked explanation
questions.explain: Synthesis means drawing together and connecting information from both texts.

questions.q: You are writing a formal letter to your local council. Which opening is most appropriate?
options: So basically the bins are a nightmare.
Bins are well annoying, sort it out.
I am writing to express my concern about waste collection in our area.
Hey, listen up about these bins!
questions.explain: A formal letter requires a clear, polite statement of purpose in Standard English.

questions.q: Addressing the reader as "you" in a persuasive article is known as:
options: Personification
Onomatopoeia
Alliteration
Direct address
questions.explain: Speaking straight to the reader using "you" is direct address.

questions.q: Which sentence best uses 'show, not tell' to convey that a character is nervous?
options: The girl was nervous because of the test.
She felt nervous and scared inside.
Her hands trembled as she gripped the pencil, her eyes fixed on the clock.
She was very nervous about the exam.
questions.explain: Showing physical detail lets the reader infer the emotion rather than stating it outright.

questions.q: Which is an effective way to vary sentence length for tension in narrative writing?
options: Use the same length throughout
Follow several longer sentences with a short, punchy one: 'He stopped.'
Use only very long sentences
Avoid full stops entirely
questions.explain: A sudden short sentence after longer ones creates emphasis and tension.

questions.q: You are writing a speech. Which feature would make it most engaging for a live audience?
options: A repeated phrase used as a rallying refrain
A bulleted shopping list
Footnotes and references
Long, unbroken paragraphs of dense detail
questions.explain: Repetition (anaphora) builds rhythm and impact, ideal for spoken delivery.

questions.q: A leaflet tells readers "Always wear a helmet and check your brakes." Its main purpose is to:
options: Entertain
Tell a story
Argue against cycling
Advise
questions.explain: Practical guidance and instructions for the reader's benefit show the purpose is to advise.
